title: This Bird Builds an Optical Illusion to Win Over One Viewer

scenes.text: This bird builds an optical illusion for an audience of one.
The male great bowerbird builds a stick avenue and puts the biggest pebbles at the back, the smallest near the entrance.
From where the female stands, far-off big objects look the same size as near small ones. It's called forced perspective.
Researchers swapped the pebbles around in fifteen bowers. Most males moved them back within days, and every one had fixed it in two weeks.
Males who built the strongest illusions won the most mates. Nobody taught him architecture.

subject: great bowerbird
description:
This bird builds an optical illusion for an audience of one.
Male great bowerbirds arrange pebbles so a female looking down the avenue sees a smaller, tidier courtyard. Males with the best illusions got the most mates.
What would you build to impress someone?
